recipe_version.title: Hawaiian Shoyu Ahi Poke Bowls with Seasoned Rice, Cucumber, Avocado, and Edamame
recipe_version.description: Cubes of sashimi-grade ahi tuna tossed in a shoyu dressing of soy sauce, sesame oil, sweet onion, scallions, ginger, and red chile flakes, served over vinegar-seasoned short-grain rice with cucumber, avocado, edamame, nori strips, and toasted sesame seeds.

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade ahi tuna
ingredients.display_name: sashimi-grade ahi (yellowfin) tuna sold for raw use

ingredients.name: toasted nori sheet
ingredients.display_name: toasted nori sheet (label lists seaweed only)

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.body: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer under the running tap, rubbing gently, until the rinse runs nearly clear, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: Combine the rice and 2 1/2 cups water in a 2-quart saucepan. Bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, then cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes; leave it covered off the heat to rest 5 minutes. The covered cooking and rest run inside steps 3 to 5 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Season the vinegar
steps.body: Stir the rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl until dissolved.

steps.title: Make the poke
steps.body: Cut the tuna into 3/4-inch cubes. In a mixing bowl stir the soy sauce, sesame oil, sweet onion, scallions, ginger, and chile flakes; fold in the tuna and keep the bowl cold while you prepare the toppings.

steps.title: Prep the toppings
steps.body: Dice the cucumber and slice the avocados, about 6 minutes. Thaw the edamame in a strainer under the warm tap, about 1 minute, and drain. Snip the nori into thin strips.

steps.title: Season the rice
steps.body: Spread the hot rice in a wide bowl and fold in the seasoned vinegar with a paddle until glossy, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.body: Divide the rice among bowls. Top with the poke, cucumber, avocado, and edamame in sections, then the nori strips and sesame seeds.

recipe_version.food_safety_note: The tuna is eaten raw. Buy tuna the fish counter sells for raw consumption (sashimi-grade, previously frozen for parasite control), keep it cold, and serve it the day it is bought. Raw fish is not advised for pregnant people, young children, older adults, or anyone with a weakened immune system.
